meta.title: PLOT TWIST!
meta.description: You create the characters. They create the chaos. A pixel-art storytelling sandbox for original characters.

language.label: Language
language.note: Only the interface changes. Your characters and stories stay in the language you wrote them in.

title.paradeLabel: A few characters waiting for a story

worlds.heading: Where does it all go wrong?
worlds.intro: Pick the world your characters live in. You can change it later.

western-fantasy.name: Western Fantasy
western-fantasy.blurb: Mossy villages, crooked castles and prophecies nobody reads to the end.

modern.name: Modern
modern.blurb: Cafés, late trains and group chats where secrets hide in plain sight.

ancient-china.name: Ancient China
ancient-china.blurb: Courtyards, roadside inns and wandering swordsmen with debts of honor.

otherworld.name: Otherworld
otherworld.blurb: Floating islands, glowing plants and rules of physics that change their minds.

studio.heading: Assemble your cast
studio.introWorld: Your story takes place in {world}. Everything saves automatically in this browser.
studio.intro: Everything saves automatically in this browser.
studio.emptyBody: Create your first original character. Who are they, and what are they hiding?
studio.deleteBody: {name} will be gone for good. This can't be undone.

portrait.title: Portrait
portrait.note: Placeholder portraits. Your own art, a pixel editor or AI portraits can plug into this frame later.

studio.methodsNote: Describe your character in words, with sliders, or both. The two are saved separately and sliders never rewrite what you wrote.

boundaries.title: Boundaries
boundaries.intro: What this character won't share, won't discuss or won't do. Trust never overrides these by itself.
boundaries.hardHelp: Hard: never crossed in play. Only editing the character here changes them.
boundaries.softHelp: Soft: avoided for now. They may open up to one person after real shared experiences, never just because someone asks again.
boundaries.empty: No boundaries written yet. Locked canon that says "never…" still counts as a hard boundary.

textPlaceholder.topic: e.g. Her childhood in the lighthouse
textPlaceholder.principle: e.g. Never cheats, even to win

boundaries.topicsHint: Comma separated, any language. A message containing one of these touches the boundary.
boundaries.topicsPlaceholder: e.g. crush, love, 喜欢, 暗恋

personality.label: Personality
personality.placeholder: Curious, impatient, kind in a loud way...

background.label: Background
background.placeholder: Where do they come from? What happened?

goals.label: Goals
goals.placeholder: What do they want more than anything?

fears.label: Fears
fears.placeholder: What would they never admit to being scared of?

habits.label: Habits & preferences
habits.placeholder: Little things they do without thinking. Favorite foods, pet peeves...

rules.label: Character rules & boundaries
rules.placeholder: Things this character would NEVER do, or topics the story should avoid.

identity.label: Identity
identity.placeholder: Role, job, title, species... e.g. apprentice cartographer

values.label: Values & beliefs
values.placeholder: What do they believe is right? What won't they compromise on?

speakingStyle.label: Speaking style
speakingStyle.placeholder: Short sentences? Big words? A catchphrase? Never swears?

canon.label: Must stay consistent
canon.placeholder: Key facts the story must never contradict. One per line.

lock.hint: Locked details are canon. The AI must keep them exactly as written.

gender.label: Gender
gender.note: Optional. Only used to refer to the character correctly. It never changes their personality, interests or behavior. Saved for this version of the character only.

builder.heading: Set the scene
builder.intro: Describe where your story begins, pick a type of place, then generate a map. Edit the words and generate again until it feels right.
builder.describePlaceholder: A cramped bookshop above a noodle stand. It always smells like rain, and the back door is locked from the inside...
builder.describeHint: Saved automatically. Chinese or English both work.
builder.quoteEmpty: No description yet. Your words will appear here.

map.drawingHint: This can take up to a minute.
map.iterateHint: Change the description and generate again for a new version.
map.needDescription: Write a description first, then generate a map.
map.unavailable: Map generation is not set up yet
map.unavailableHint: Add OPENAI_API_KEY to .env.local and restart the app to turn it on. Until then the preview shows built-in art.
map.outdated: You changed the description or place type since this map. Generate again to see the new version.
map.keepHint: You're still looking at your current map until the new one is ready.
map.pixelGridCopyHint: Older maps are high-resolution pictures. This makes a copy on the game's pixel grid, as a new version. The original stays as it is, and it costs nothing.
map.pixelGridFailed: The pixel-grid copy couldn't be made in this browser.

edit.selectHint: Drag over the map to select the area you want to change.
edit.adjustHint: Drag the box to move it, or drag a corner to resize it.
edit.selectionLabel: Selected area. Arrow keys move it, Shift + arrow keys resize it, Delete clears it.
edit.example2: Turn this area into a flower garden.
edit.example3: Replace this empty space with a pond and wooden fence.
edit.keepHint: Everything outside the box stays as it is. Each edit is saved as a new version.
edit.needSelection: Select an area on the map first.

builder.sampleNotice: This is the game's built-in sample art for “{place}”. It was not made from your description. Generate a map to draw one from your words.

play.noWorldBody: Every story needs somewhere to happen. Pick a world first.
play.demoNotice: You haven't created anyone yet, so a demo cast is standing in.
play.selectInScene: Select a character in the scene.
play.keyboardHint: Keys: ← → choose · Z talk · X observe · C wait · V twist · L log · Esc pause

log.empty: Nothing has happened yet. Talk to someone.

play.aiFallback: AI writing didn't work ({reason}), so a built-in line was used.

bubble.finish: {name} is speaking. Show the full line

sidebar.noBonds: No bonds yet. Events between characters build them.

test.title: Emotion & movement test
test.intro: Pick a character in the scene (◀ ▶ or tap them), then press a button. Everything here goes through the same rules as the story, so a refused action tells you why.
test.reactDesc: Personality, bond and feeling decide how they move. Off: effect only.
test.needTwo: Add a second character to try walking toward someone.

reasons.unknown_target: the other character isn't on stage
reasons.no_room: there's no free spot next to them
reasons.cornered: there's nowhere to back away to, so they turned away instead
reasons.player_command: you're steering them right now, so their own reaction waits
reasons.outranked: they're busy with something more important (your command or the story)
reasons.not_allowed: that isn't something they can do with it

notes.already_close: already close, so they just turned to face them
notes.shortened: only a short step was possible
notes.nearby: that exact spot was blocked, so they're going to the nearest reachable spot

play.sampleCast: Add the sample cast (Mira, Wren, Tobi)
play.detailsHint: Everything about {name}. The conversation above keeps going while this is open.

scene.intro: The {place} is quiet. Too quiet. Pick someone and see what happens.
scene.silent: ...  (They have nothing to say yet. Give them goals or fears in the Character Studio.)
scene.observeEmpty: You look at {name}. They're still a sketch.
wait: Time passes in the {place}. Nobody admits they're waiting for something.
A quiet moment in the {place}. {name} glances your way.
Somewhere in the {place}, something creaks. Everyone pretends not to notice.

a.name: Juniper
a.appearance: They keep tucking a pencil behind their ear and forgetting it's there.
a.personality: Curious, impatient, kind in a loud way.
a.goals: Find out who left the letter on my doorstep.
a.fears: That the letter was meant for someone else.
a.relationships: Owes Rook a favor. Won't say what for.

b.name: Rook
b.appearance: Long coat, tired eyes, very clean boots.
b.personality: Dry humor, says less than they know.
b.habits: Rook taps the table twice before answering any question.
b.goals: Keep everyone out of trouble. Mostly Juniper.
b.fears: Being needed and not showing up.

load.heading: Save file
load.intro: Your game is saved in this browser automatically.
load.emptyBody: Start a new game to create your first save.

myWorlds.heading: My Worlds
myWorlds.intro: Every world keeps its own characters, relationships, memories, maps and story. Nothing in one world ever changes another.
myWorlds.copyFailed: This world couldn't be copied: the browser's storage is full. Deleting a world you no longer need will make room.
myWorlds.copyUnreadable: This world's save couldn't be read, so it wasn't copied. Nothing was changed.
myWorlds.deleteBody: “{name}” will be removed from this browser, along with its characters, relationships, memories, story and maps.
myWorlds.deleteSafe: Your other worlds are not touched.
myWorlds.emptyBody: Create a world to start your first story.
myWorlds.migrated: Your earlier save is now the world “{name}”. The original save is kept as a backup in this browser.

settings.title: Settings
settings.textSpeedDesc: How fast lines type out in speech bubbles and the dialogue panel. Click or tap a line to show it all at once.
settings.crtDesc: Old-TV lines over the whole screen.
settings.motionDesc: Turns off page transitions and bouncing.
settings.offlineReady: Everything except the AI features works offline after your first visit. Saves live in this browser.
settings.offlineFuture: AI analysis, AI dialogue and pixel generation need an internet connection and API keys on the server.
settings.dangerDesc: Deletes your world, characters and story log from this browser.
settings.eventFrequencyDesc: How often waiting turns into a plot twist.
settings.aiStoryDesc: Let the AI write dialogue and conversation replies when it's set up. Off means built-in lines only.
settings.testPanelDesc: Shows buttons under the dialogue in Play Mode to trigger every emotion and movement by hand.
settings.behaviorDebugDesc: Shows why each character chose what they did: personality, feelings, relationship, memories and every option's weight. Hidden from players.
settings.relationshipInspectorDesc: Developer tool: long-term relationship values, stages, milestones and why each change was accepted or refused.
settings.aiCheckNote: This checks the key and model without making anything. Running out of credits only shows up when something is generated.

aiModes.balanced: Balanced (AI only when you start it)

sliders.title: Personality sliders
sliders.intro: Each slider is a tendency, not a rule. Leave any of them unset and the game reads your written profile instead.

conflicts.title: Review differences
conflicts.intro: Your written profile and the sliders seem to disagree here. Both can be true at once, so you decide. Nothing changes until you pick.
conflicts.item: You wrote “{words}”, but the {trait} slider is at {value} ({lean}).
conflicts.keepBothHint: It's nuance. The AI will treat it as a situational difference.
conflicts.none: No differences between your text and the sliders.

memories.confide: the time {with} opened up to them
memories.temptation: the day they almost broke a rule
memories.fearTrigger: the moment their fear came close

analysis.title: Behavior analysis
analysis.intro: The analysis reads your written profile, sliders, relationships, rules, memories and current mood, and turns them into a behavioral profile. You review it before it affects the story.
analysis.unavailableHint: Add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY to .env.local and restart the app. The built-in analysis works offline in the meantime.
analysis.needInput: Write something in the profile or set a slider first.
analysis.stale: You've edited this character since this analysis. Run it again to include the changes.
analysis.notUsedYet: Until you approve an analysis, play uses your sliders and written profile directly.

local.summaryNeutral: {name} is balanced on every slider so far, so the written profile carries the most weight.

decision.mixed: Careful with big choices, quick with small ones.

social.out: Seeks people out and fills silences.
social.in: Keeps a small circle and needs time alone.
social.mixed: Comfortable in a group, but picks their moments.

triggers.act: When there's a chance to do something
triggers.cooperate: When a problem is too big for one person

variations.confront: With people they trust, they argue more gently.
variations.deflect: If it truly matters, they face it eventually.
variations.withdraw: Around someone they trust, they open up instead.
variations.comfort: When they're hurting themselves, they may need comfort back.
variations.joke: In a real crisis the jokes stop.
variations.investigate: With close friends they ask instead of assuming.
variations.act: When someone else is at stake, they slow down.
variations.cooperate: If trust breaks, they go it alone.

local.conflictNote: Your text and this slider point different ways. Both can be true; review it on the Personality tab.

errors.invalid_output: the AI's answer didn't pass validation
errors.rate_limited: too many requests, try again in a moment
errors.failed: the AI service had a problem
errors.too_large: the image is larger than 8 MB
errors.bad_type: only PNG, JPG or WebP images work
errors.timeout: it took too long to answer
errors.busy: a reply is already being written
errors.limit: the conversation limit was reached, try again later
errors.unsupported: this image service can't edit part of a map
errors.billing: the AI account has run out of credits or hit its spending limit (add credits in the provider's billing page, then try again)
errors.ai_off: AI is switched off in the current AI mode (Offline). The built-in lines are used instead
errors.budget: the development AI budget for this session is used up (raise it or reset it in the API Usage dashboard)

sprite.title: Pixel character
sprite.intro: Upload a picture of your character and turn it into a standing sprite (32×32) and portrait (96×96) in the game's pixel style.
sprite.standingOnly: Standing pose only. Walking animations aren't part of this version.
sprite.fileHint: PNG, JPG or WebP · up to 8 MB
sprite.referenceNote: When you save, a small copy is kept with the portrait so you can see what it was made from. Your original file is never changed.
sprite.permission: I made this image or have permission to use it.
sprite.generatingHint: This can take up to a minute.
sprite.unavailableHint: Add OPENAI_API_KEY to .env.local and restart the app to turn it on. You can still use the quick conversion below.
sprite.convertHint: Shrinks your picture straight into sprite pixels. Works best on drawings with a plain background.
sprite.saved: Saved to {name} and your sprite library.
sprite.libraryEmpty: Sprites you save appear here, and any character can reuse them.

fileErrors.type: That file type isn't supported. Use PNG, JPG or WebP.
fileErrors.size: That image is larger than 8 MB.

spec.ok: Meets the sprite spec (32×32, hard edges, limited palette).
spec.empty: Almost empty: try turning off background removal

sprite.nothingFound: Couldn't find a character in this image. Try turning off “Remove plain background”.
sprite.savedNewVersion: Saved to {name}. The new picture was added as a new portrait version.

editor.title: Pixel editor
editor.canvas: Sprite pixels, 32 by 32. Use the pointer to draw.
editor.note: Edits change the sprite. The portrait stays as it was.

colorPicker.usePrevious: Go back to the previous color
colorPicker.limitedNote: Limited palette: every color snaps to the nearest of these {n} colors.
colorPicker.savedEmpty: Save colors you like to find them again. They're remembered in this browser.

pantone.unavailable: No licensed Pantone library is installed, so no Pantone match is shown. Pantone codes are proprietary; the game won't guess one.
pantone.unverified: Unverified approximation ({source}). Not an official Pantone match.

warm: Oh, I don't mind telling you. “{text}”
teasing: “{text}” Don't laugh. Okay, you can laugh a little.
probing: Why do you want to know? ...“{text}” Your turn.
Before I answer, who's asking? ...All right. “{text}”
rambling: So, okay, long story, but basically: “{text}” ...and that's the short version!
“{text}” Wait, did I already tell you that? Anyway!
Oh! That reminds me: “{text}” Where was I?
formal: “{text}” I trust that answers your question.

happy: Something has put {name} in a good mood. {detail}
irritated: {name}'s jaw is set. Best tread lightly. {detail}
excited: {name}'s eyes are bright with some new idea. {detail}
suspicious: {name} is watching everyone a little too carefully. {detail}
embarrassed: {name} is pretending very hard that nothing happened. {detail}

confide: {other} sits down next to {name}. “Can I tell you something? {text}”
Out of nowhere, {other} admits something to {name}: “{text}”
{other} lowers their voice. “{name}, I've never said this out loud. {text}”
argument: It starts small, then {other} tells {name} they're wrong about ‘{text}’.
{name} and {other} end up on opposite sides, and it's about ‘{text}’.
misunderstanding: {name} catches half a sentence from {other}: “...can't trust them...” Wait. Them who?
{name} sees {other} quickly hide a note. Probably nothing. Probably.
{other} laughs right as {name} walks in. Was that about {name}?
kindness: {other} quietly leaves something warm next to {name}.
{other} fixes the thing {name} was struggling with, without making a fuss.
{other} saves {name} the good seat in the {place}.
tease: {other} does a spot-on impression of {name}. Everyone saw.
“Oh no,” says {other}, “{name} has an idea again.”
askHelp: {name} needs a hand with this: ‘{text}’. {other} is right there.
{name} realizes they can't manage ‘{text}’ alone. They look at {other}.
A chance to get closer to ‘{text}’ appears, but it needs two people. {other} is nearby.
rivalry: {name} and {other} reach for the same thing in the {place} at the same moment.
Only one of them can win this. {name} and {other} both know it.
{other} gets the credit for something {name} did. Or did they?
rumor: Someone in the {place} whispers a rumor about {other}. {name} hears every word.
Word around the {place} is that {other} has been hiding something.
temptation: An easy shortcut appears, but it would mean going against this: ‘{text}’.
Someone offers {name} exactly what {name} has always wanted, on one condition: bend ‘{text}’. Just once.
No one is watching. {name} could ignore ‘{text}’ and nobody would know.
goalStep: Something in the {place} might bring {name} closer to ‘{text}’.
A clue about ‘{text}’ turns up where {name} least expected it.
{name} gets a real chance to work on ‘{text}’.
fearTrigger: Something in the {place} brushes too close to {name}'s fear: ‘{text}’.
For a moment the {place} feels exactly like ‘{text}’. {name} goes still.
A small, ordinary thing reminds {name} of ‘{text}’.
memoryEcho: A smell, a sound, and {name} is back in {memory}.
quietMoment: A quiet moment. {name} does the usual: ‘{text}’.
Nothing happens, and {name} slips into an old habit: ‘{text}’.
The {place} goes quiet. You notice something about {name}: ‘{text}’.

western-fantasy: A crow lands nearby and very clearly says “{name}”. Then it leaves.
Every candle in the {place} leans the same way for a moment.
A prophecy scroll blows past. The last line is smudged, as usual.
modern: Every phone in the {place} buzzes at once. Same message: “soon”.
The lights flicker, and a song nobody chose starts playing.
A delivery arrives addressed to {name}. Nobody ordered it.
ancient-china: A paper crane lands on {name}'s sleeve, carrying a sealed message.
A wandering swordsman bows to {name} as if they've met before.
The temple bell rings once, though no one is near it.
otherworld: Gravity takes a short break. Everything floats an inch, then settles.
A glowing plant in the {place} turns to follow {name}.
A small creature trades {name} a pebble for a button and runs off.

interior: {name} finds a note tucked under a loose floorboard.
Behind a cupboard, {name} finds a key that fits nothing here.
{name} finds a drawer that wasn't there yesterday.
street: {name} spots a dropped map with one street circled.
A stall {name} has never noticed is selling exactly one thing.
{name} finds a coin stamped with an unfamiliar face.
wilderness: {name} finds footprints that stop in the middle of a field.
Under a mossy stone, {name} finds a tiny carved door.
{name} finds a ribbon tied around a tree, very deliberately.
ruins: {name} uncovers a mural of someone who looks a lot like {them}.
{name} finds a lantern that's still warm.
A loose stone reveals a hollow with a sealed letter inside.
dreamscape: {name} finds a door standing on its own, slightly open.
{name} finds a clock with no hands, ticking anyway.
{name} finds a photograph of a day that hasn't happened yet.

progress: It works. A real step forward.
Against the odds, it pays off.
setback: It doesn't go to plan. Not even close.
A setback. Annoying, but not the end.

withdraw: ...I'm going to go stand over there.
Can we talk about this later, {other}?
comfort: That makes sense. Thank you for telling me.
You don't have to carry that alone, {other}.
joke: Well, that's going in my memoir.
If we survive this, I'm telling everyone.
investigate: Wait. What exactly do you mean, {other}?
Hm. Who else knows about this?
Something doesn't add up. Walk me through it.
act: Don't stop me. I've already decided.
cooperate: Okay, {other}. Let's figure it out together.
We're better at this as a team, {other}.

joke: Of course this happens to me.
Ten out of ten, very weird.
investigate: Hold on. Let me look closer.
There's a reason for this. I'll find it.
act: No time to think. Going for it!
I'll just... try it and see!
cooperate: I should tell the others about this.
This is a job for more than one person.

up: Something between {name} and {other} gets a little warmer.
{name} and {other} understand each other a bit better now.
down: Things between {name} and {other} get a little colder.
A small crack appears between {name} and {other}.

short: Hi! I didn't see you there.
Oh, hello. Good to see you.
Hey, you're here early.
full: Hey! I was hoping I'd run into you today.
There you are! I've been wanting to tell you something.
Hi! Come here, look what I found on the way over.

terse: Wait. Can I ask you something?
short: Hey, can I tell you something?
Do you have a minute? I had an idea.
Walk with me for a bit?
full: Okay, I have to tell you about this, it's been stuck in my head all morning.
Perfect timing! I need someone to hear this plan before I talk myself out of it.
Come here, come here. You won't believe what I just figured out.

short: Sorry, I was just leaving.
Can this wait? I'm in the middle of something.
I'd rather not, right now.
full: I don't really feel like talking at the moment, if that's okay.
Let's not do this today. I need some air.
I'm sure it's important, but I can't right now. Really.

short: Oh! I didn't expect that.
Wait, really?
You scared me!
full: Oh! I genuinely did not see that coming.
Wait, wait. Say that again, I think I misheard.
Whoa. Okay. That's not what I thought you'd say.

short: I'm really glad you came.
You always make this place feel nicer.
I saved you a seat. Obviously.
full: Honestly? Today got a lot better the second you showed up.
I was just thinking about you, and here you are.
Stay a bit? Everything's easier with you around.

short: Can you not, just for once?
That's really getting on my nerves.
I heard you the first time.
full: I'm trying very hard to stay calm right now, and you are not helping.
Every single time. Do you even hear yourself?
Okay, that's enough. I'm done pretending this is fine.

short: What do you mean by that?
Why are you telling me this?
Wait, what's this about?
full: Sorry, I need to understand this first. What exactly are you asking me?
Hang on. Why now, and why me?
Before I answer, can you tell me what's really going on?

short: I'll think about it.
Okay… what is it?
That depends.
full: I'm listening. I just want to be sure I understand first.
Let's go slowly, if that's alright with you.
Maybe. I'd like to know a bit more before I decide.

short: Ha! You wish.
Careful, I might start liking you.
Is this a bribe? Because it's working.
full: Oh, absolutely. And next you'll tell me the islands float because they're happy.
Ha! Say that again, slower, so I can remember it forever.
Alright, alright, you win this round. Enjoy it while it lasts.

short: I had it under control.
That's not what happened.
You don't know the whole story.
full: I did exactly what anyone sensible would have done, so let's not pretend otherwise.
Before you lecture me, maybe ask why I did it.
I don't need you to tell me how to do my job.

short: What do you want from me?
Don't think that changes anything.
I don't need your approval.
full: If you're being nice, you want something. So what is it?
Flattery won't get you anywhere, if that's the plan.
Save it. I know exactly how you talk about me when I'm not around.

short: Anyway, did you see the sky today?
Let's talk about something else.
So! How about that map?
full: Right, moving on. Has anyone checked whether the bridge is still floating?
Okay, enough about me. What have you been up to?
Funny you say that. Unrelated, but have you eaten yet?

short: Say that to my face.
Want to settle this properly?
You really think you can beat me?
full: Fine. Race me to the lighthouse and we'll see who's right.
If you're so sure, let's put it to the test. Right now.
You keep talking. I'd rather see you actually do it.

short: You're right. I'll fix it.
Fair point. I didn't think of that.
Okay. Let's do it your way this time.
full: I don't love hearing it, but you're right. I'll do better.
That's fair. I got carried away. Thanks for saying it.
Alright. We do this together, properly, and we argue about it later.

short: That's kind of you. Thank you.
Thanks. That means a lot.
Oh. I didn't expect that. Thanks.
full: Thank you, really. I wasn't sure anyone noticed.
That's a kind thing to say. I'll remember it.
Thanks. Coming from you, that actually matters.

retreat: {name} edges away, putting a little space between themself and {other}.
stay_silent: {name} presses {their} lips together and stays quiet.

affection: {name} looks away from {other} a moment too quickly.
sadness: Something in {name}'s face closes, just for a second.
{name} blinks a few times and says nothing about it.

debug.title: Behavior debug
debug.intro: Why characters do what they do. Pick an event, fire it, and read every option's weight. Developers only.
debug.sandboxNotice: Sample scenario on the real stage. Sample characters only: nothing here is saved to your story.
debug.seedPlaceholder: e.g. 42 — same seed + same state = same result
debug.seedNote: Fixed seed: firing again from the same state repeats the result. State changes (feelings, cooldowns) still make later results differ.
debug.empty: No decision yet. Fire an event, or play: every reaction in the game shows up here.
debug.noStrongReason: no single strong reason; picked among close options
debug.rejected: Rejected by hard limits (before any dice)
debug.notApplicable: {n} other actions don't apply to this kind of event.
debug.labelNote: The label is context only; behavior reads the numbers.
debug.legend: p = personality, e = feelings, r = relationship, m = memories, c = place & distance, pref = the character's own tendencies. × means both must be true.

scenarios.introFriend: Same introvert approached by a close friend
scenarios.extroFearedRival: Extrovert approached by a feared rival
scenarios.proudComplimentedByEnemy: Proud character complimented by an enemy

talk.hint: Drag a character onto someone to talk, onto an object to use it, or onto the floor to walk there.
talk.hintTouch: Touch and hold a character, then drag onto someone, an object, or the floor.
talk.chooseHelp: Tap someone on the stage, or pick a name:

notices.unreachable: {name} can't find a way to {other}. Something is in the way.
notices.blocked: {name} can't get past someone standing in the way to {other}. Try moving them first, or pick someone closer.
notices.noRoom: There's no free space to stand next to {other}.
notices.busy: {name} is in the middle of something. Try again in a moment.
notices.emptySpace: To start a conversation, drop {name} onto another character.
notices.unreachablePlace: {name} can't get there. Something is in the way.
notices.nearby: That spot is blocked, so {name} is going as close as possible.

topics.betrayal: Ask {other} why they broke your trust

memory.helped: the time we helped each other

soft: {other}… are you doing okay?
How are you feeling, {other}? Really?
bold: Hey {other}! How are you holding up?
So, {other}, how's your day going?

soft: You seem down, {other}. Want to sit with me for a bit?
Whatever it is, {other}, you don't have to carry it alone.
bold: Okay, enough gloom, {other}. Let's find something good about today.
Chin up, {other}! I've got a terrible joke ready if you need it.

soft: Is something worrying you, {other}?
You can tell me what's on your mind, {other}. Only if you want to.
bold: What's eating at you, {other}? Out with it.
Something's bugging you, {other}. What is it?

soft: About what happened between us… can we talk about it, {other}?
I keep thinking about our disagreement, {other}.
bold: We need to talk about what happened, {other}.
Let's clear the air, {other}. That fight's still bugging me.

soft: {other}, I'm sorry about before. I didn't handle it well.
I owe you an apology, {other}.
bold: Look, {other}, I was out of line. Sorry.
Okay. I messed up, {other}. I'm sorry.

soft: Why did you do it, {other}? I need to understand.
I haven't forgotten what you did, {other}.
bold: Explain yourself, {other}. Why did you betray me?
Did you think I'd just forget, {other}?

soft: I think I could beat you this time, {other}.
Want to see who's better at this, {other}?
bold: Bet you can't keep up with me, {other}!
Rematch, {other}. Right now.

soft: Do you remember {memory}, {other}?
I was thinking about {memory}, {other}.
bold: {other}! I still think about {memory}.
Remember {memory}, {other}? Good times.

soft: I like how you see things, {other}.
You're really good at this, {other}. I mean it.
bold: {other}, you're honestly kind of amazing.
Nobody does it like you, {other}!

soft: Is that your thinking face, {other}? It's very serious.
Did you sleep at all, {other}? Your hair says no.
bold: Wow, {other}, did you get dressed in the dark?
Still slower than me, {other}?

soft: Can I tell you something, {other}? Just between us.
{other}, there's something I haven't told anyone.
bold: {other}, I trust you, so here goes.
Okay, secret time, {other}. Don't laugh.

soft: {other}, could you help me with something? It matters to me.
I'm stuck on something important, {other}. Would you help?
bold: {other}, I need a hand. You in?
Help me out with something, {other}? It's a big deal for me.

soft: What are you hoping for, {other}? What do you want most?
Do you have something you're working toward, {other}?
bold: So what's your big plan, {other}?
Tell me, {other}: what are you really after?

soft: Um, hi. I'm {name}. I don't think we've really met.
Hello. I'm {name}. You're {other}, right?
bold: Hi! I'm {name}. And you're {other}, right?
Hey, we haven't met properly. I'm {name}!

interior: It's cozy in here, isn't it, {other}?
Have you noticed how quiet this room gets, {other}?
Someone should really tidy this place up.
street: Did you see that stall on the corner, {other}?
I like watching people go by. Don't you, {other}?
wilderness: It's so open out here, {other}. Hear that wind?
Careful where you step, {other}. Things grow fast out here.
I could stay out here all day.
ruins: Who do you think built all this, {other}?
Stay close, {other}. I don't trust these walls.
dreamscape: The sky keeps changing color. Is it just me?
I feel like I've been here before, {other}.

western-fantasy: Did you hear? The guild posted a dragon bounty.
They say the old wizard's tower lit up again last night, {other}.
modern: Did you see the news this morning, {other}?
Apparently the café on the corner is closing. Can you believe it?
ancient-china: I heard a wandering swordsman passed through the city gate today.
They say the magistrate is holding a poetry contest, {other}.
otherworld: Word is the floating islands drifted closer overnight, {other}.
Someone saw a slime wearing a hat by the crystal fields.

refuse_polite: I'd rather not talk about that, {other}.
That's not something I want to get into.
Let's leave that one alone, if you don't mind.
refuse_firm: No. I'm not talking about that.
That stays with me, {other}. Don't ask.
explain_boundary: I already said no, {other}. Some things I keep to myself, and that's one of them.
Asking again won't change my answer. That's a line for me.
I meant it the first time. That isn't up for discussion.
deflect: Is that really what you want to talk about? Pass.
change_subject: Let's talk about something else. Anything else.
So… did you see the weather out there?
question_intent: Why do you want to know?
Who's asking, you or someone else?
express_discomfort: You keep asking, {other}. I don't like it.
I've said no twice now. This is making me uncomfortable.
Please stop pushing. It's not okay.
hesitate: …I'm not sure I want to say.
I… don't know. Let me think about it.
disagree: I think you're wrong about this.

playArea.title: Play area
playArea.intro: The picture can't tell the game where the floor or the furniture is, so mark it here. Paint the floor green where characters may walk, draw a box around furniture and things they can use, and add a few starting spots.

hints.floor: Drag over the picture to paint where characters can walk.
hints.wall: Drag to remove floor: walls, the top of the picture, anything nobody should stand on.
hints.object: Drag a box around a piece of furniture or something to use. Click a box to change it.
hints.spawn: Click to add a place where characters start. Click one again to remove it.
hints.walk: Drag over the picture to paint where characters can walk. The brush is measured in map cells, so zooming never changes how much it paints.
hints.block: Drag to remove floor: walls, water, anything nobody should stand on.
hints.rect: Drag a box around a piece of furniture or something to use. Click an object to select it.
hints.pen: Click to place points around the object. Click the first point (or Finish) to close the outline. Backspace removes the last point, Esc cancels.
hints.edit: Drag a point to move it, drag inside to move the whole shape, click a + to add a point. Select a point and press Delete (or double-click it) to remove it.
hints.anchor: Click where a character should stand to use the selected object.
hints.pan: Drag to move around the zoomed picture. The mouse wheel scrolls it too.
